title: Encoded PowerShell attack on WORKSTATION6 - pgustavo user
summary: An encoded PowerShell command executed on WORKSTATION6 under user pgustavo, launched by wmiprvse.exe. The command decoded to disable Script Block Logging and AMSI, then download and execute code from external IP 10.10.10.5 (outside company network ranges). User pgustavo normally logs into WORKSTATION5, making this cross-host activity anomalous.
evidence: PowerShell -enc flag detected on WORKSTATION6 at 04:14:55
Parent process wmiprvse.exe launched by svchost.exe under NETWORK SERVICE
Decoded command shows: disable Script Block Logging, bypass AMSI, download from http://10.10.10.5, execute downloaded code
IP 10.10.10.5 rated suspicious - private address not in company known ranges
User pgustavo normally uses WORKSTATION5, but activity occurred on WORKSTATION6
Command chain: whoami.exe executed after PowerShell, confirming reconnaissance
related_to_prior: ALERT-001 is the first alert in this investigation chain

recommended_actions.action: Disable pgustavo account and force password reset
Block external IP 10.10.10.5 at perimeter firewall
Full forensic analysis of WORKSTATION6 PowerShell logs and downloaded artifacts
Review all hosts pgustavo has accessed in last 7 days for similar anomalous behavior
Enable Script Block Logging and AMSI monitoring if disabled

title: Encoded PowerShell execution via WMI lateral movement on WORKSTATION6
summary: At 04:14:55, user pgustavo logged network from 172.18.39.5 and WMI (wmiprvse.exe) launched PowerShell with an encoded command (-enc). The decoded command reveals intent to disable script block logging, bypass AMSI, download and execute code from 10.10.10.5:80. PowerShell subsequently connected to that IP. This follows ALERT-001 (same user, same host) and indicates account compromise for lateral movement and defense evasion.
evidence: Network logon by pgustavo from 172.18.39.5 at 04:14:55.108 on WORKSTATION6
WmiPrvSE.exe launched powershell.exe as parent process at 04:14:55.050
PowerShell command included -enc flag with base64-encoded payload
Decoded command shows: disables ScriptBlockLogging, bypasses AMSI, downloads from web, runs downloaded code, uses proxy credentials
PowerShell connected to 10.10.10.5:80 at 04:14:57.513 shortly after launch
whoami.exe executed from PowerShell at 04:15:14.694 confirming active shell
IP 172.18.39.5 rated as internal; 10.10.10.5 is an unreachable/internal destination
User pgustavo is a Domain (lab) user with normal host WORKSTATION5, not WORKSTATION6 — indicates credential use from atypical system
Attack chain continues from ALERT-001: same user, same host, encoded PowerShell pattern
related_to_prior: ALERT-001: Same user pgustavo, same host WORKSTATION6 — this is the second stage of an account compromise attack chain, moving from initial encoded PowerShell to WMI-based lateral movement

recommended_actions.action: Isolate WORKSTATION6 from network immediately to prevent further lateral movement
Reset credentials for user pgustavo and enforce MFA
Block traffic to/from 10.10.10.5 at perimeter firewall
Audit all other hosts pgustavo has accessed in last 24 hours for similar WMI/encoded PowerShell patterns
Review and restore ScriptBlockLogging settings if disabled by the encoded command
Deploy AMSI monitoring/alerts on all PowerShell processes if not already enabled

title: Encoded PowerShell C2 Beacon on WORKSTATION6 by pgustavo
summary: User pgustavo executed an encoded PowerShell command (-enc flag) that connected to external IP 10.10.10.5:80. The decoded command disables script block logging and AMSI, downloads and runs code from the web — consistent with C2 beacon activity. This is the third confirmed attack event in a chain starting with ALERT-001 (encoded PowerShell) and ALERT-002 (WMI lateral movement), both also involving pgustavo on WORKSTATION6.
evidence: powershell.exe launched with -enc flag by parent process WmiPrvSE.exe
decoded command disables ScriptBlockLogging and AMSI bypass, downloads from web, runs downloaded code
connection to 10.10.10.5:80 from src_ip 172.18.39.6 (not in company network ranges)
IP 10.10.10.5 rated suspicious as private address outside known company ranges
user pgustavo logged in from 172.18.39.5 to WORKSTATION6 prior to beacon
two prior confirmed alerts (ALERT-001, ALERT-002) involving same user and workstation with encoded PowerShell
whoami.exe executed after beacon connection confirming active shell
related_to_prior: Continuation of attack chain: ALERT-001 (encoded PowerShell) → ALERT-002 (WMI lateral movement) → ALERT-003 (C2 beacon). Same user pgustavo, same host WORKSTATION6, escalating techniques.

recommended_actions.action: Terminate powershell.exe process and all child processes
Reset credentials for user pgustavo and audit all active sessions
Block outbound connections to 10.10.10.5 at firewall/proxy
Full malware scan of WORKSTATION6 with updated signatures
Review all other hosts accessed by pgustavo for similar indicators
Audit and restore ScriptBlockLogging settings if disabled
